paper.title: UI-Mem: Self-Evolving Experience Memory for Online Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Agents
paper.central_claim: A hierarchical, abstracted, self-evolving experience memory (workflows, subtask skills, failure patterns as parameterized templates) integrated into online GRPO via stratified group sampling, dynamic dropout curriculum and guidance-aware reward lets GUI agents reach higher AndroidWorld/AndroidLab success than vanilla/dense-reward/replay RL and transfer to unseen apps.

missing_sections: Figures 5, 6, 7 (component analysis, unseen-app bars, training curves) are images without numeric text

evidence.quote: Unlike traditional replay buffers, our memory accumulates structured knowledge, including high-level workflows, subtask skills, and failure patterns.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated retained object: a hierarchical memory of workflows, subtask skills and failure patterns (non-weight), as opposed to raw replay.

evidence.quote: The memory is stored in a vector database indexed by the embeddings of task and subtask descriptions, enabling efficient similarity search at scale.
evidence.support_explanation: Persistence location of the retained store: a vector DB read by later rollouts.

evidence.quote: If a similar entry is found, we merge the new experience by updating the associated statistics: increasing the success count
evidence.support_explanation: The only described write rule: similarity-based merge (count update) or append; no deletion/retirement/rollback rule is described in the main text.

evidence.locator: Sec 4.1 Reward Evaluation and Experience Extraction
evidence.quote: we adopt a two-stage text-based verification pipeline: we first use Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct
evidence.support_explanation: Feedback signal for both RL reward and memory admission is an LLM pipeline (VLM description then DeepSeek-V3 state verification), not the benchmark checker.

evidence.quote: the Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct+DeepSeek-V3 settings reaches an F1 score of 0.902
evidence.support_explanation: Validity of the training-time judge is reported (accuracy 0.900 elsewhere in text) but the labelled evaluation set size/provenance is not stated; ~10% judge error flows into memory admission.

evidence.quote: we collect task instructions from AMEX ( Chai et al., 2024 ) , AndroidLab ( Xu et al., 2024a ) , and UI-Genie ( Xiao et al., 2025 ) , filtering for tasks compatible with core apps in our emulator environment.
evidence.support_explanation: Training instructions are drawn from AndroidLab (also an evaluation benchmark) and filtered to apps in the emulator; no overlap audit against AndroidWorld/AndroidLab test tasks is reported.

evidence.quote: To increase task diversity, we employ GPT-4o to augment these seed instructions
evidence.support_explanation: Training queries (256) are GPT-4o-augmented from seed instructions; external teacher knowledge enters through data and extractors (Seed1.8, DeepSeek-V3).

evidence.quote: we utilize the annotated trajectories to generate subtask definitions, which are subsequently refined through the self-evolving loop during training.
evidence.support_explanation: The initial memory structure is seeded from annotated (human/privileged) trajectories rather than starting from an empty store.

evidence.quote: The UI-Mem-4B model achieves a success rate of 58.2%, significantly outperforming the vanilla Qwen3-VL-4B (45.3%)
evidence.support_explanation: Headline AndroidWorld gain for 4B (45.3 -> 58.2); single reported value, no variance.

evidence.quote: UI-Mem-8B with memory retrieval achieves a state-of-the-art success rate of 71.1%
evidence.support_explanation: 8B with inference-time memory (UI-Mem star) reaches 71.1; without memory retrieval Table 1 lists 66.8 (8B) and 62.5/58.2 for 4B with/without.

evidence.locator: Sec 4.4 Comparison with RL Training Paradigms
evidence.quote: Experience Replay improves training stability (56.5%), but remains limited to replaying static historical data
evidence.support_explanation: Matched Qwen3-VL-8B comparison table (Table 3): vanilla GRPO 53.0, +progress reward 57.3, +replay 56.5, inference-time prompting 52.6, UI-Mem 66.8.

evidence.quote: disabling the memory update reduces performance to 62.9%, highlighting the importance of continuously refining the memory pool during the training progress.
evidence.support_explanation: Only quantitative store-update ablation (62.9 vs full); the metric/model is read from Figure 5 which is not available as text, so the exact pairing with 66.8 is our inference.

evidence.quote: Moreover, replacing our abstracted memory with raw experience results in a significant performance drop (58.2%).
evidence.support_explanation: Abstraction-vs-raw ablation; remaining component values (hierarchy, no stratified sampling) are only given qualitatively.

evidence.quote: we select five held-out apps from AndroidLab that are completely absent from our training set: Bluecoins, Cantook, Maps.me, Pi-Music, and Zoom.
evidence.support_explanation: Strictest holdout in the paper; per-app numbers live only in Figure 6 (not available as text).

evidence.quote: The baseline frequently collapses to near-zero when sampled groups consist entirely of failures, resulting in vanishing gradient.
evidence.support_explanation: Mechanism evidence for stratified sampling: intra-group reward variance (Figure 7b) is the claimed link between guidance mixture and learnability; qualitative description only.

evidence.quote: the unguided policy is trained to match the performance of guided subgroups, thus gradually transferring the knowledge encoded in the external memory into the agent’s internal parameters.
evidence.support_explanation: Claimed internalization mechanism (policy trained with strong/weak/no guidance within the same GRPO group).

evidence.quote: For failure patterns, we use a recency bias to prioritize recent error diagnoses, ensuring that the guidance reflects the agent’s latest policy behavior.
evidence.support_explanation: Staleness handling for failure patterns is a retrieval-time recency weight, not a retirement rule.

evidence.quote: ensuring that the system effectively prioritizes robust workflows and discards unstable strategies over time.
evidence.support_explanation: Claimed discarding of unstable strategies; Algorithm 2 only sorts by UCB and updates counts, so discarding is by ranking not by an explicit removal gate (our reading of Algorithm 2).

evidence.quote: Despite their effectiveness, these approaches lack mechanisms to transfer reusable experience across tasks, failing to address the fundamental bottleneck of generating high-quality trajectories in the first place.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: replay and dense-reward GUI RL methods lack cross-task experience transfer; related work does not discuss agent memory/skill-library lineages.

evidence.quote: The benchmark comprises 138 tasks simulating daily user interactions such as managing events, editing notes, and retrieving information.
evidence.support_explanation: AndroidLab test size 138 (AndroidWorld 116 tasks per same section): one task is about 0.7-0.9 points, so differences of a few points are a handful of tasks; no CI or seeds are reported.

evidence.quote: Despite the overall effectiveness of our memory guidance, there are remaining failure modes due to unexpected grounding errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Failures are reported only as a single qualitative case; no failure counts or denominators.

evidence.quote: We train both models for five epochs with a learning rate of
evidence.support_explanation: Training budget stated (5 epochs, G=4, 256 queries) but no GPU-hours, emulator-hours or API-call counts for the reward model (72B VLM + DeepSeek-V3), Seed1.8 extractor and DeepSeek-V3 template matching.

evidence.quote: Experiments on challenging GUI benchmarks demonstrate that UI-Mem significantly outperforms baselines in both sample efficiency and success rate, with strong cross-task generalization enabled by reusable experience transfer.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim as stated (scope: AndroidWorld/AndroidLab, Qwen3-VL 4B/8B).

gap.author_gap: Online GUI RL suffers sparse reward/credit assignment and repeated cross-task errors; replay and dense-reward methods lack cross-task experience transfer.
gap.checked_gap: Real, concrete bottleneck (zero-variance GRPO groups, Figure 7b description). The fixed non-weight object is the raw-trajectory replay buffer, replaced by an abstracted hierarchical store. Nearest neighbors are checked only inside GUI-RL (replay, dense reward); agent memory/skill-library lines (workflow memory, reflection stores, skill libraries) are not discussed in this paper, and no neighbor source text is pinned for this paper, so neighbor claims remain unchecked.
gap.lineage: experience replay (MobileRL-style) / dense step reward -> memory-guided exploration with abstracted templates
closest_adjacent: Experience Replay in GUI RL (Xu et al. 2025, Lu et al. 2025a)
gap.residue: Whether abstracted memory beats stronger plain baselines (longer context, nearest-neighbor retrieval) and agent-memory systems is untested.
gap.stakes: sample efficiency and early-training success in long-horizon GUI RL
gap.method_response: Hierarchical parameterized memory plus stratified guidance gives positive-reward anchors and cross-task transfer.
gap.remaining_gap: No retirement/validation of stored entries, privileged seeding from annotated trajectories, unaudited overlap between AndroidLab-derived training instructions and the AndroidLab benchmark.

G.reason: Concrete bottleneck (zero-variance sparse-reward groups, cross-task repeated errors) and fixed object (raw replay buffer) are identified, but nearest agent-memory/skill neighbors are not examined and residual boundaries are thin.

M.reason: Mechanism chain is reconstructible: abstracted memory -> stratified guidance gives within-group outcome diversity -> unguided policy trained toward guided success; prediction (variance non-zero, unguided policy catches up) is checkable. Assumption that judge-labelled successes are reliable stays weak.

X.reason: Read path is explicit (Algorithm 1) and merge/append/UCB/recency are specified, but retention is only judge-verdict plus dedup, with no admission test, retirement, versioning or rollback; curriculum/UCB/dedup hyperparameters are missing.

E.measurement.reason: Benchmarks use programmatic state checks (AndroidWorld) and AndroidLab metrics; training-time judge accuracy/F1 vs baselines is reported, though its labelled set is undescribed and ~10% error enters memory.

E.causality.reason: Matched Qwen3-VL-8B arms (GRPO, +progress, +replay, prompting) and component ablations exist, but the claimed gain bundles four interacting mechanisms plus external teacher models (Seed1.8, DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4o) with no toggle of the conditioning alone and no teacher-knowledge control.

E.holdout.reason: Memory is built on training queries and applied to benchmark tasks, and a five-app unseen test is run (figure-only). AndroidLab appears among training-instruction sources while AndroidLab is also evaluated, with no overlap audit.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes are stated (116/138 tasks) and one failure case is shown, but every result is a single run with no CI, seeds or fold repeats; gaps of 3-5 points are a few tasks.

E.cost.reason: No GPU/emulator hours, API-call counts or latency for the 72B-VLM + DeepSeek-V3 reward pipeline, Seed1.8 extractor and retrieval LLM; baselines carry no stated budget.
